Senior Civil Judge, Ramangara, Dismissing The Claim
Petition For Compensation.

This Appeal, Coming On For Hearing, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment
In this appeal, the petitioners have challenged the judgment and award dated 16.06.2015 in M.V.C.No.114/2013 passed by the Addl. Senior Civil Judge, Ramanagara ('the Tribunal' for short).
2. For the sake of convenience, the rank of the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are, on 10.05.2012 at about 11:20 pm, son of petitioners by name Irfan Pasha Pasha, the deceased, borrowed the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05/EF-2460 belonging to the respondent No.1, riding it on Nagarabhavi Ring- road in heavy rains, due to rain a Santro car going ahead has applied the sudden brake; in order to NC: 2023:KHC:41046 avoid hitting against Santro car, he applied sudden brake to the motor cycle, due to which fell down on the road and at that time, a canter came behind and ran over his body, killing him at the spot.
The petitioners being the dependants have approached the Tribunal for grant of compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Claim was opposed by the Insurance Company.
The Tribunal after taking the evidence, by impugned judgment, dismissed the claim petition.
Aggrieved by the same, the petitioners have filed this appeal on various grounds.

4. Heard the arguments of Sri. Raju. S, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri. B. Pradeep,
learned counsel for Insurance Company of the motor cycle.

5. It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners that when a claim is made under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, there NC: 2023:KHC:41046 is no burden on the petitioners to prove the negligence on part of the rider; there was no fault on part of the deceased in the accident and in order to avoid hitting against the Santro car, he applied brake, but he fell down due to heavy rain, a canter ran over his body, killing him at the spot.
Hence, the petitioners are entitled to claim compensation and he sought for assessment of compensation under structured formula.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that the accident was tailored on his own by the deceased; there is involvement of the canter, hence Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act is not applicable.
Much apart, the deceased was riding the motor cycle at the time of accident by borrowing it from respondent No.1.
He has stepped into the shoes of the owner and there cannot be any claim by the owner against himself is not permissible.
The Insurance Company NC: 2023:KHC:41046 under the terms of the policy has to indemnify the liability of the insured.
Here in this case, there is no liability on the insurer as he himself was involved in the accident and the order of dismissed by the Tribunal is proper and he supported the impugned judgment.
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on both sides and also perused the materials on record.
8. The material on record did point out that there was an accident involving the motor cycle.
The deceased borrowed the motor cycle from respondent No.1 and rided it in the Ring Road in heavy rain.
In order to avoid hitting against Santro car, he applied brake, fell down on the road, the incoming canter killed him at the spot.
Claim is against the owner and insurer of the motor cycle.
The Santro car or the canter are not arrayed as parties to the claim petition.

In a case of this nature, the Hon'ble Apex Court in Ramakhiladi and Anr. -Vs- United India Insurance Company and Anr.1 laid down that if the deceased is a permissible user or borrower of a motor cycle which he was riding, then the parties are bound by the contract of Insurance.

entities.text: Ramakhiladi and Anr. -Vs- United India Insurance Company and Anr.1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The liability of the Insurance Company shall be as per the terms and conditions of the contract of Insurance.

At paragraphs No.5.5, 5.6 and 5.8, it is held as follows:
"5.5

It is true that, in a claim under Section 163A of the Act, there is no need for the claimants to plead or establish the negligence and/or that the death in respect of which the claim petition is sought to be established was due to wrongful act, neglect or default of the owner of the vehicle concerned.
It is also true that the claim petition under Section 163A of the Act is based on the principle of no fault liability.

However,
at the same time, the deceased has to be a third party and cannot maintain a claim under Section 163A of the Act against the owner/insurer of the vehicle which is borrowed by him as he will be in the shoes of the owner and he cannot maintain a claim under Section 163A of the Act against the owner and insurer of the vehicle bearing registration No. RJ 02 SA 7811.
In the present case, the parties are governed by the contract of insurance and under the contract of insurance the liability of the insurance company would be qua third party only.
In the present case, as observed hereinabove, the deceased cannot be said to be a third party with respect to the insured vehicle bearing registration No. RJ 02 SA 7811.

AIR 2020 SUPREME COURT 527 NC: 2023:KHC:41046 There cannot be any dispute that the liability of the insurance company would be as per the terms and conditions Smt. Noorjan vs Sri. Syed Imran on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145690131/
3 of the contract of insurance.

entities.text: Smt. Noorjan vs Sri. Syed Imran
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As held by this Court in the case of Dhanraj (supra), an insurance policy covers the liability incurred by the insured in respect of death of or bodily injury to any person (including an owner of the goods or his authorized representative) carried in the vehicle or damage to any property of a third party caused by or arising out of the use of the vehicle.
In the said decision, it is further held by this Court that Section 147 does not require an insurance company to assume risk for death or bodily injury to the owner of the vehicle."

"5.6 In view of the above and for the reasons stated above, in the present case, as the claim under Section 163A of the Act was made only against the owner and insurance company of the vehicle which was being driven by the deceased himself as borrower of the vehicle from the owner of the vehicle and he would be in the shoes of the owner, the High Court has rightly observed and held that such a claim was not maintainable and the claimants ought to have joined and/or ought to have made the claim under Section 163A of the Act against the driver, owner and/or the insurance company of the offending vehicle i.e. RJ 29 2M 9223 being a third party to the said vehicle."
"5.8
However, at the same time, even as per the contract of insurance, in case of personal accident the owner-driver is entitled to a sum of Rs.1 lakh.
Therefore, the deceased, as observed hereinabove, who would be in the shoes of the owner shall be entitled to a sum of Rs.1 lakh, even as per the contract of insurance.

However, it is the case on behalf of the original claimants that there is an amendment to the 2nd Schedule and a fixed amount of Rs.5 lakh has been specified in case of death and therefore the claimants shall be entitled to Rs.5 lakh.
The same cannot be accepted.

In the present case, the accident took place in the year 2006 and even the Judgment and Award was passed by the learned Tribunal in the year 2009, and the impugned Judgment and Order has been passed by the High Court in 10.05.2018, i.e. much prior to the amendment in the 2nd Schedule.
In the facts and NC: 2023:KHC:41046 circumstance of the present case, the claimants shall not be entitled to the benefit of the amendment to the 2nd Schedule.

At the same time, as observed hereinabove, the claimants shall be entitled to Rs.1 lakh as per the terms of the contract of insurance,
the driver being in the shoes of the owner of the vehicle."
9.1.

In view of the above, it is clear that the petitioners in order to maintain a petition under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act, the deceased has to be a third-party and instant petition cannot be maintained against the owner/insurer of the motor cycle which is borrowed by the deceased.
The deceased, will be in the shoes of owner.
It is further held that the claimants are entitled to claim compensation under the terms of the contract.
Ex. R1
/ copy of policy of insurance points out that the policy covers the own damage of the vehicle, liability to third-party and personal accident cover to the owner-driver of Rs.1,00,000/-.
Now, the deceased is the borrower of the motor cycle from respondent No.1.
By virtue of it and by applying the above settled principles, he will enter into the shoes of R.C. NC: 2023:KHC:41046 owner.
Hence, the legal representatives of the owner are entitled to claim the P.A. cover issued by the Insurance Company under the terms of the policy.

sentences.text: the deceased to be treated as a deemed owner of the motor cycle, the petitioners being his dependants are entitled to claim personal accident cover of Rs.1,00,000/- only.

Since the deceased was not a third-party to the motor cycle, by virtue of the deemed ownership, the petition under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act is not maintainable, the Tribunal is right in dismissing the claim petition.
The Tribunal has lost sight of the settled principles and also the terms of Ex.R1/policy that there is a personal accident cover for owner-rider of the motor cycle to an extent of Rs.1,00,000/-.
The petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- from the Insurance Company under the terms of contract of insurance.
